config.title: Event Handling

intro.title: Event Handling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive button that responds to user clicks. You'll learn how to handle events in Vue by using the v-on directive to listen for user actions. The core concept is event handling, which allows your application to react to user input like clicks. You'll work with Vue's template syntax and methods to update the page content dynamically when the button is pressed.
intro.usecase: Event handling is fundamental to every interactive Vue application, from simple form submissions to complex dashboard interactions. In real products, you'll use event handling when users click buttons in e-commerce checkouts, toggle filters in data tables, open modal dialogs, or submit search queries. As a Vue developer, you'll constantly wire up @click, @submit, and @input handlers to make UI components respond to user actions, creating the responsive experiences modern web applications require.

objectives: Bind Vue event listeners to DOM elements using the v-on directive
Implement inline event handlers to execute JavaScript expressions
Construct methods to handle events with reusable logic
Apply event modifiers to control default browser behavior
Integrate event handling with data properties to update the UI reactively
Manipulate event objects to access target properties and values
Configure event handling for form inputs to capture user data

steps.title: Import Vue and ref from 'vue'
steps.instruction: Import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package to use Vue's reactivity system.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a module
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue and ref modules are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'EventHandlingDemo' using the <script setup> syntax and a template that returns a single root <div> element.
steps.hint: Use the <script setup> tag to define a Vue component. The template should contain a single root element, typically a <div>.
steps.analogousExample: // Example of a basic Vue component with script setup
steps.expectedOutcome: The component structure is defined with a script setup block and a template containing a root <div>.
successCriteria: A Vue component named 'EventHandlingDemo' is created with <script setup> and a template that returns a single root <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both the <script setup> block and a <template> with a single root <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Remember to use <script setup> for the component logic and <template> with a single root element like <div>.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, declare a reactive count variable using ref and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Use const count = ref(0) to create a reactive reference with an initial value of 0.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a reactive variable
const message = ref('Hello');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive count variable ready to track changes.
successCriteria: A reactive count variable is declared using ref with an initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref(0) to initialize the count variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: Declare a const count = ref(0) inside the <script setup> section.

steps.title: Define an increment handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> block, define a function named incrementCount that increases the count value by 1.
steps.hint: You can create a regular JavaScript function that modifies the reactive count variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named incrementCount is defined that will be used to handle button click events.
successCriteria: The incrementCount function is defined and correctly increments the count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named incrementCount and increments count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The incrementCount function isn't defined correctly. Check the function name and that it modifies count.value.

steps.title: Define a reset handler function
steps.instruction: Define a function called resetCount that sets the count value back to 0.
steps.hint: Create a function that assigns 0 to count.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A resetCount function is defined that resets the count to 0.
successCriteria: The resetCount function is defined and sets count.value to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named resetCount and sets count.value to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The resetCount function isn't defined correctly. It should set count.value to 0.

steps.title: Add a heading to display the count
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add an h1 element that displays the current count value using template interpolation.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display the reactive count value in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a reactive value in Vue template

Current value: {{ myValue }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain an h1 element that shows the current count value.
successCriteria: An h1 element is added inside the template div that displays the count value using template interpolation syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the correct syntax for template interpolation with double curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 element with template interpolation for the count value is missing. Remember to use {{ count }} inside the h1 element.

steps.title: Add an increment button and wire its click event
steps.instruction: In the template, add a button element with the text 'Increment' and wire its click event to the increment function using @click.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to call the increment function when the button is clicked.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="increment">Increment</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Increment' appears in the UI, and clicking it will increase the count value.
successCriteria: The template contains a button element with text 'Increment' and an @click directive that calls the increment function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and the @click directive is properly set to call the increment function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or the click event isn't wired correctly. Check that you've added a button with @click="increment" and the text 'Increment'.

steps.title: Add a reset button and wire its click event
steps.instruction: Define a reset handler function that sets the count back to 0.
steps.hint: Create a function named reset that updates count.value to 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: The reset handler function will be defined and ready to be used with a button.
successCriteria: A function named reset is defined that sets count.value to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've defined the reset handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function sets count.value to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Define a function named reset that sets count.value to 0.

steps.title: Add a decrement handler function
steps.instruction: Define a function called decrementCount that decreases the count value by 1.
steps.hint: Create a function that modifies the reactive count state by decrementing its value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A decrementCount function is added to handle decreasing the count.
successCriteria: The decrementCount function is defined and correctly decreases count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function name is exactly 'decrementCount' and it decreases count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement handler function is missing or incorrect. Try defining a function named decrementCount that modifies count.value.

steps.title: Add a decrement button and wire its click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Decrement' inside the template, and wire its click event to call the decrementCount handler using @click.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element after the reset button in the template. Use @click to bind the decrementCount function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button with click handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A third button labeled 'Decrement' appears in the UI, and clicking it decreases the count by 1.
successCriteria: The template contains a button element with text 'Decrement' and an @click attribute that calls decrementCount.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the text 'Decrement' and uses @click="decrementCount" to call the handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement button is missing or not properly wired. Add a <button> with text 'Decrement' and @click="decrementCount" in the template.
